gitCommit.body:
docs: the 2026-09-15 session-3 record, SDUI §147, and tomorrow's agenda (#342)

RECORD (CLAUDE.md) — the headline Mukesh asked for, the three defects he found
by USING the live page, the fourth I found by reading what the page renders,
and iOS 1.0.7 submitted. Close-out read LIVE from prod: 759fbbeb, isProd:true,
prod ref. /newsroom TTFB 8.34s/10.01s -> 0.31s.

⚠️ The perf number carries an honest limit, recorded rather than glossed: every
reading is a single sandbox-proxy request against an idle page. What makes the
comparison sound is that the baseline used the same tool over the same path,
taken deliberately after the merge and before the build landed.

SDUI §147 — the port-contract record. iOS impact classified FOUR ways over
17cec0fe..759fbbe, machine-proven:
  (A) native binary: project.yml + both release_notes.txt — and they GOT their
      build, consumed by the 1.0.7 submission the same day. Nothing parked.
  (B) server-authored spec: NONE.
  (C) runtime-fetched content/**: NONE.
  (D) App<->external boundary: NONE — zero files under src/app/api/.

§147a — the three web modules grep to ZERO in the iOS tree, but "0 hits" is not
"iOS unaffected": InternalLinkRouter returns .webView(.newsroom), so the app
renders both surfaces inside a WKWebView and every web fix reaches iOS users on
their next page load with no build.

§147b — a NEW contract shape, and it runs the opposite way to most rows here: a
WEB fix whose whole justification is a NATIVE renderer's behaviour. WKWebView
does not paint a first frame for preload="metadata" with no poster, so the
video tiles were empty boxes; #t=0.1 makes it seek and render that frame. When
a page is reached through .webView(...), the PWA is not the only benchmark —
WKWebView is a second renderer with its own defects, and it is the one most of
our customers use.

§147c — the release-notes trap, an App<->Apple boundary that nearly bit, plus
the DO-NOT-FIRE legacy workflow that sorts first under `ls | grep ios`.

AGENDA (2026-09-16) — refreshed at the session-3 close. Items 2 and 7 are done;
item 3, the carrier registry, is named as the one thing the day did not reach
and is carried a second time. Two watches added: /newsroom under the reel's
traffic tomorrow, and the empty-state copy confirmation. The pattern bullet
gains the day's two shapes — a control that works but leads nowhere is a broken
control, and a label built for a chip is not a word you can drop into a
sentence.

npm run verify green — 550 files / 7102 tests. Docs-only.
